newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Shell Sri Lanka gas strike ends.
newsitem.headline: Shell Sri Lanka gas strike ends.

text.p: A six-day strike at Sri Lanka's monopoly gas distributor, owned by the Royal Dutch/Shell Group, was called off on Tuesday, state radio said.

The strike at Shell Gas Lanka Ltd by union labour, demanding the reinstatement of nine employees suspended for violating safety rules at Colombo port when gas was being unloaded, brought gas distribution to a halt in the Indian Ocean island.
The strike caused gas shortages for city and suburban consumers, forced some restaurants to shutter their doors and industries relying on gas to consider stopping production.
Shell management and labour union officials were not immediately available for comment.

The Sri Lanka Broadcasting Corporation said Shell agreed to withdraw the suspension of the nine employees and asked workers to observe safety rules while union labour agreed to return to work and give adequate notice of strikes.
The deal came after talks between Shell management, labour union leaders and Labour Minister Mahinda Rajapakse, it said.
Talks on Monday between the All Ceylon Commercial and Industrial Workers Union and the Employers Federation of Ceylon representing Shell failed to resolve the strike.

Shell Overseas Investment BV, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Royal Dutch/Shell Group, bought a majority stake in the state-owned gas monopoly in October last year for $37 million under the government's programme to privatise state enterprises.
The company is currently embroiled in a controversy with the government after it increased the price of domestic gas twice in one year, in apparent violation of the privatisation deal.

The Public Enterprises Reforms Commission, which handles privatisations, has said Shell was given a five-year gas distribution monopoly under the privatisation deal on condition that prices could only be raised by 10 percent a year.
